key_insight: VETime fuses 1D temporal signals with 2D vision representations so a single zero-shot model can detect both fine-grained point anomalies and long-range contextual anomalies, avoiding the usual trade-off between temporal precision and global context.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between temporal models (good at pointwise localization) and vision models (good at global patterns) by resolving temporal alignment and coarse-grained detection issues for zero-shot time-series anomaly detection.
method: Render time-series windows into 2D visual representations (e.g., spectrograms / recurrence plots / windowed renderings) to expose global patterns to vision backbones.
Fuse pre-trained 2D vision features with 1D temporal features via a temporal-vision alignment module and multi-scale feature fusion to preserve pointwise localization and global context.
Perform zero-shot anomaly scoring using pre-trained vision embeddings combined with temporal consistency/distance metrics (no target anomaly labels required).
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy anomaly detectors that require no anomaly-specific training while improving detection of both immediate and contextual anomalies—reducing labeling costs and improving robustness for monitoring and alerting systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: time series -> 2D rendering -> vision encoder + temporal encoder -> alignment & fusion -> anomaly score

paper_title: VETime: Vision Enhanced Zero-Shot Time Series Anomaly Detection
paper_authors: Yingyuan Yang, Tian Lan, Yifei Gao, Yimeng Lu, Wenjun He
